subject: physics
question_text: State and prove the law of conservation of energy in the case of a freely falling body.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 6 LONG ANSWER — and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material carries the same question in its own Unit 6 Long Answer set, so both sources agree this is an 8-mark form. The split across the steps is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty. AI physics check 2026-08-24: formulas, signs, numbers and claims verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; corrections applied to explanation text (why / common_mistakes / memory_tip); a factually wrong marked line was corrected.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The statement
lines: Energy can neither be created nor
destroyed. It can only be converted from
one form into another, and the total
energy of an isolated system stays constant.
steps.margin_note: Both halves earn marks — "neither created nor destroyed" AND "total stays constant".
steps.why: The proof that follows is one worked case of this statement: the potential energy is not lost as the body falls, it becomes kinetic energy.
common_mistakes: Stating only that energy changes form, without saying the total is constant.
Using 'closed' where the exact word is 'isolated' — a system exchanging neither energy nor matter. If energy can enter or leave the system, the total inside can change.

recall.must_convey: That energy is neither created nor destroyed, only converted, and the total stays constant.
accept: energy can neither be created nor destroyed
it changes from one form to another
total energy remains constant
energy create cheyyalemu destroy cheyyalemu
reject: at A the potential energy is m g h

steps.memory_tip: The statement has two halves: energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes form.

steps.label: The three points
steps.margin_note: Mark A, B and C with h, x and (h − x). The proof is three heights and this is where they are defined.
steps.why: Every line below says "at A", "at B", "at C". Without the figure those names mean nothing and the marks for them are hard to award.
common_mistakes: Drawing the fall but not labelling x and (h − x), so the B calculation has no distances to use.

recall.must_convey: That a figure is drawn showing the body at A, B and C with h, x and (h − x) marked.
accept: draw the figure with A B and C
mark h and x and h minus x
A B C points tho figure geyyali
reject: at A the potential energy is m g h

steps.memory_tip: Draw three labelled points on one vertical line: A at height h, B after falling x, C at the ground.

steps.label: At A — the top
steps.margin_note: Take each point the same way: KE, then PE, then their sum. The pattern is what makes the proof readable.
steps.why: At the top all the energy is potential. This is the value every later total has to match.
common_mistakes: Writing KE = ½mv² at A without setting u = 0.

recall.must_convey: That at A the kinetic energy is zero and the total is mgh.
accept: at A kinetic energy is zero
potential energy is m g h
total at A is m g h
A daggara KE zero, PE mgh
reject: at C the potential energy is zero

steps.memory_tip: At A everything is potential: total = mgh. This number must repeat at B and C.

steps.label: At B — after falling x

lines.text: At B (after falling a distance x):

lines: Height above the ground = (h − x), so
Using v² − u² = 2as with u = 0, a = g,
steps.margin_note: B is the step worth the most. The x cancels — show that line, do not just assert the total.
steps.why: B is the only point where both energies are non-zero, so it is the real test: the mgx gained as kinetic is exactly the mgx lost as potential.
common_mistakes: Using height h instead of (h − x) for the potential energy at B.
Forgetting the ½ when squaring, giving KE = 2mgx.

recall.must_convey: That at B, PE = mg(h − x), KE = mgx from v₁² = 2gx, and the total is again mgh.
accept: at B potential energy is m g h minus x
v squared equals two g x
kinetic energy is m g x
total at B is again m g h
B daggara kuda mgh vastundi
reject: at A kinetic energy is zero

steps.memory_tip: B is the real test: PE = mg(h − x), KE = mgx from v² = 2gx — the total is mgh again.

steps.label: At C — the ground
lines: Using v² − u² = 2as with s = h:
steps.margin_note: Same three lines as before. At C the energy is all kinetic — the mirror image of A.
steps.why: At the ground every joule that was potential at A is now kinetic. That is the conversion the law describes, seen at its extreme.
common_mistakes: Leaving a potential-energy term at C when the height is zero.

recall.must_convey: That at C the potential energy is zero and the kinetic energy is mgh.

reject: at B potential energy is m g h minus x

steps.memory_tip: At C everything is kinetic: v² = 2gh gives KE = mgh.

steps.margin_note: Put the three totals side by side, then say what it proves. Do not leave the reader to compare them.
steps.why: A proof is not finished until the three separate results are put together. The equality IS the law for this case.
common_mistakes: Calculating all three totals and never writing the line that compares them.

recall.must_convey: That E at A, B and C are all equal to mgh, so the energy is conserved.

steps.memory_tip: Finish by writing the three totals side by side: mgh at A = at B = at C.
